task: creative: Little Lamps story Charles and the Prayers at the Windows

errors.what: en.wikipedia.org API returned 429 on the first request; the ?action=raw page URL worked. web.archive.org reset the connection and franciscanmedia.org returned 403.
errors.fix: used archive.org's own metadata and download endpoints for Giussano's Life, which worked

integrity_issues.what: The first draft of the post claimed a source check (Charles feeding people at street corners) that the run never ran.
integrity_issues.fix: Caught on re-read before commit and replaced with a sentence about a check that was actually run (the speech impediment in Giussano).

doc_friction.issue: The 400 MB audio cap and the 'skip the podcast option' rule conflict with PRODUCTION.md and docs/reports/2026-11-13-audio-cap-is-stale.md, which say audio has been served from jsDelivr since 2026-10-24 and the cap now only guards git history. creative_due.py still reports 577/400 and says text only. A run cannot tell which one wins without asking the owner.

deviations.why: The Borromeo proposal named the barefoot procession as the scene for small children. Giussano's plague chapters had gentler, better-attested scenes (prayers at the windows, the little book, the curtains).
deviations.did: Made the windows the centre of the story and told the procession briefly and gently.
deviations.result: A story with no frightening image; each scene is cited by chapter in the note.

notes: Project: hearth-and-horizon, Little Lamps shelf; piece: charles-and-the-prayers-at-the-windows (1,376 words, text only; audio folders 577 MB over the 400 MB cap). creative_due.py drew little-lamps. certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
